items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: UDesign action control with semantic variants, press and pending feedback, and accessible touch targets.
items.docs: The pending prop disables the control, reports aria-busy, and swaps in a spinner while preserving the button's width so the layout does not jump when the work starts. The label turns transparent, never hidden, so it stays the accessible name: a pending button needs no aria-label. Press treatment is per-variant: a neutral surface darkens to the pressed role while a solid surface has no deeper solid role to move to, and every variant keeps a non-motion colour signal since --motion-press-scale collapses to 1 under reduced motion. See DESIGN.md.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: Semantic UDesign badge with independent tone and visual treatment.
items.docs: A badge holds one line, so a status in a table column or a toolbar stays whole. Where a label can be wider than its container, such as a card on a phone, pass wrap: the label wraps inside the container instead of running past its edge (ban 29). See DESIGN.md.

items.name: alert
items.title: Alert
items.description: Accessible message container covering every UDesign semantic tone.
items.docs: An Alert is part of the page and is not a live region: a notice shown with the page is met in reading order. Pass live (role="status") when its appearance is the news, such as a result, or live="assertive" (role="alert") for an error that stops the work. An explicit role wins. See DESIGN.md "Feedback primitives".

items.name: card
items.title: Card
items.description: Composable UDesign surface for grouped content.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: Mobile-safe text input using UDesign interaction roles.

items.name: textarea
items.title: Textarea
items.description: Resizable multiline input using UDesign interaction roles.

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.description: Accessible Radix select styled with UDesign semantic roles.
items.docs: An open Select sets pointer-events and a scroll lock on <body>, so every choice makes the browser restyle the whole page. For a long list, a dense grid of many selects such as one per table row, or a phone, use native-select, which shares this trigger's look and states. See DESIGN.md "Choosing a select".

items.name: native-select
items.title: Native Select
items.description: The platform's own select, styled as SelectTrigger: for long lists, dense grids of many selects, and phones.
items.docs: NativeSelect shares SelectTrigger's tokens, height, radius, focus ring, hover, press, disabled and invalid states, and its chevron. Choose it over Select for a long list, a dense grid of many selects such as one per table row, or a phone, where the system picker serves better: a native select changes nothing on <body> when it opens, while a Radix Select makes the browser restyle the whole page on every choice. className and style land on the wrapper that holds the chevron; every other prop and the ref reach the <select>. See DESIGN.md "Choosing a select".

items.name: choice-group
items.title: Choice Group
items.description: One choice shown as buttons: sizes and options in explicit columns, or colour swatches, with a note under the group.
items.docs: A radio group of buttons with one Tab stop. The arrow keys move and choose, and the group stops them, so a listener on the page, such as a gallery's, never sees them. Each button holds its label alone; a choice that cannot be had is disabled, dashed and struck through, and says so in words (unavailableLabel, English by default). Say what the buttons do not carry, a surcharge or what cannot be had, in note, which the group points at with aria-describedby. Columns come from container queries in dist/tokens.css of the same release: one row when every choice gets 4rem, otherwise rows of one count, the last at most one shorter, never one alone, never a cell under the touch target. The group takes its width from its parent. See DESIGN.md "Choosing one of a few".

items.name: table
items.title: Table
items.description: Responsive data table with keyboard-scrollable overflow and touch-safe rows.
items.docs: TableRow has no pressed state: a <tr> cannot take focus or a key press, so press styling would promise a click the keyboard cannot make. A clickable row is Pressable, not a styled <tr>. See DESIGN.md.

items.name: icon-button
items.title: Icon Button
items.description: Icon-only action requiring an accessible label and minimum touch target.

items.name: progress-ring
items.title: Progress Ring
items.description: Domain-neutral completion ring for a bounded set, with a visible numeric readout so meaning never depends on color or arc angle alone.

items.name: rolling-consistency-chip
items.title: Rolling Consistency Chip
items.description: Trailing-window consistency count (e.g. '4 of the last 7'). Replaces the streak concept entirely - tone never varies with the count.

items.name: moment
items.title: Moment
items.description: Bounded, in-place reaction wrapper for a closed loop, capped at intensity 2. Gamification-exclusive: inert without data-game="on" (ADR-0001). Not included in the core bundle - install it only in a repository that has opted in.
items.docs: Intensity is capped at 2: intensity 3 (screen-level celebration, particle bursts, overlays) does not exist in this design system and must never become expressible through this component. Moment renders no icon or text of its own; the caller's children carry the actual state change, which is what still communicates closure when the animation is removed under reduced motion. See DESIGN.md.

items.name: status-badge
items.title: Status Badge
items.description: Domain-neutral status marker with tone, icon, and busy-state support.

items.name: metric-card
items.title: Metric Card
items.description: Data readout separating positive, negative, and neutral movement from status semantics.

items.name: empty-state
items.title: Empty State
items.description: Actionable empty collection state with optional icon and call to action.

items.name: responsive-collection
items.title: Responsive Collection
items.description: Explicit desktop and mobile render slots for ergonomic collection layouts.

items.name: spinner
items.title: Spinner
items.description: Busy indicator for an action in flight. Stops turning under reduced motion rather than disappearing, so the state stays visible.
items.docs: The ring renders whether or not it turns: under reduced motion the spin animation drops but the shape stays a visible busy indicator. Pass label to announce the wait to assistive technology, or omit it when a parent already reports aria-busy. See DESIGN.md.

items.name: skeleton
items.title: Skeleton
items.description: Loading placeholder sized to the content it stands in for, so arrival does not shift the layout.
items.docs: Size the skeleton to mirror the dimensions of the content it stands in for. A fallback of a different height causes a jump on arrival, which reads worse than the blank pause it replaced. See DESIGN.md.

items.name: pressable
items.title: Pressable
items.description: Clickable surface for a card, row, or list item. A real button, so keyboard activation and the accessible name come from the platform.
items.docs: Renders a real button for a clickable card, row, or list item, so Enter, Space, focus, and the accessible name come from the platform instead of a div with an onClick. Uses the subtle press scale: the standard control press scale reads as a layout bug across a full-width surface. See DESIGN.md.

items.name: page-canvas
items.title: Page Canvas
items.description: The presentation page shell: the page scrolls, content sits in a centered column, a section can run edge to edge, and a header and a contact footer frame the page.
items.docs: Use for a screen presented to someone, under data-design="presentation". PageCanvas wraps the document; PageSection gives each block a centered column and generous vertical space, and variant="band" runs a raised surface edge to edge. PageHeader opens the page: the lockup as its children, at most one action at right, one row a touch target high whoever is on the page. ContactFooter ends it with the public contact the page supplies (address, phone, email); the design system holds no business data. Hierarchy comes from space and elevation. An operations screen uses AppShell instead. See DESIGN.md "Profiles" and "Components".

items.name: app-shell
items.title: App Shell
items.description: The operations page shell: a persistent sidebar, a toolbar, and panes that scroll inside a fixed viewport.
items.docs: Use for a screen operated by someone, under data-design="operations". Compose AppShell > AppShellSidebar (put a nav inside, laid out as a column) + AppShellToolbar + AppShellPanes > AppShellPane (give each an aria-label). From md the viewport is fixed and panes scroll, and the toolbar's controls go compact on a desktop mouse. The toolbar keeps its own height at every width and the panes take the rest, so a short page never stretches the toolbar. Below md the page scrolls and the sidebar hides: render the same nav in a Sheet (side="left") opened from a menu Button first in the toolbar, as examples/operations-queue.tsx does. Panes butt against each other on hairlines: no gap, no elevation. A presentation screen uses PageCanvas instead. See DESIGN.md "Profiles".

items.name: core
items.title: UDesign Core
items.description: Complete UDesign new-york component and pattern source set.
items.docs: UDesign core installed. Before you build: every interaction shows a visible change within 100ms; every interactive element has a pressed state; every async control shows pending in itself (Button has a pending prop); a clickable row or card is Pressable, never a div with onClick; durations and easings come from --motion-* roles. Emphasis: one accent-filled control per screen, never inside a repeated row, card, or list item. Read AGENTS.md, then DESIGN.md.
